quests.conceptTitle: Pre-Reading Schema Activation: Why Peak Tickets Cost More
quests.passage: Rail companies charge higher fares at rush hour for a practical reason, not just to make money. Trains are fullest between 7 and 9 a.m., and extra carriages are expensive to run for only two hours a day. By making peak travel pricier, companies encourage flexible passengers to travel later, which spreads the crowd across more trains. Passengers who can start work at ten often save a surprising amount.
